summary: Implemented the ADR-028 byte-limit display mapping and the settings-page display/store wiring (goal G6, phase 16 task 16.1). src/ArrTags/Configuration/ByteLimitField.cs and ByteLimitUnits.cs are the code-owned mapping for the seven byte-denominated limits: fixed binary unit (MB, 1048576 bytes; KB, 1024 bytes for WebhookMaxPayloadBytes), fixed step S (64 KiB for ProviderResponseLimitBytes/SourceArtifactLimitBytes/DerivedArtifactLimitBytes, 1 MiB for RenderCacheQuotaBytes/ArtifactStorageQuotaBytes/InventoryCacheMaxBytes, 1 KiB for WebhookMaxPayloadBytes), fixed precision P (4 for the 64-KiB-step fields, else 0), and the unchanged OperationalLimits byte bounds/defaults. FormatDisplay renders bytes at P with trailing zeros trimmed; FormatRange renders the unit-labelled range (e.g. '0.0625 - 64 MB'); TryParseDisplay accepts at most P fractional digits, parses the decimal as a scaled integer, computes bytes = round(scaled * U / 10^P), and rejects any value that is not an exact step multiple (0.1 MB computes 104858 bytes and is rejected). The conversion does not re-check the byte range: that stays owned by the unchanged OperationalLimits.Validate and the page's native min/max. config.html now declares the seven inputs in the field unit (type=number, min/max/step in MB/KB, unit-labelled label and 'Valid range: ...' description), mirrors the mapping in the byteLimitFields table, renders stored bytes through byteLimitToDisplay on pageshow, converts displayed values through byteLimitToBytes (same algorithm plus the explicit 'bytes % definition.stepBytes !== 0' rejection) in readByteLimitValues before the save request, rejects an invalid value with a native validity message, and writes only converted bytes into config.Limits[...]. The persisted XML, OperationalLimits, PluginConfiguration, and the save path are untouched; no endpoint or dependency is added. Tests: ByteLimitUnitsTests (103 cases) and ByteLimitSettingsPageTests (5 structural cases) = 108 new cases; default suite Failed 0 / Passed 1727 / Skipped 63 / Total 1790 (baseline Failed 0 / Passed 1619 / Skipped 63 / Total 1682). Eight test-sensitivity probes were run and reverted (see test_sensitivity). Documentation: changelog task entry, PLANS.md checkbox, state.json task done/report; render-docs-state up to date; check-docs PASS before the worker report was persisted. Host-guarded run not performed: ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR is unset in this environment.

interpretations.question: Does the display->store conversion also re-check the field's byte range?
interpretations.chosen: No. ByteLimitField.TryParseDisplay enforces syntax, at-most-P fractional digits, and step alignment only; the byte range stays owned by the unchanged OperationalLimits.Validate and by the page's native min/max constraints.
interpretations.basis: ADR-028 clause 1 fixes the conversion algorithm (scaled integer -> round -> step rejection) and states the internal OperationalLimits byte-range validation is unchanged; the new check introduced by this task is the step-multiple check.
interpretations.impact: An out-of-range displayed value is still rejected (natively before submit and server-side by the unchanged validator); the conversion itself makes no range claim, so no persisted or user-visible semantics change.

interpretations.question: What happens to a persisted off-step byte value (possible from the pre-16.1 page, which accepted any in-range integer) when the page displays and saves it?
interpretations.chosen: It loads and is used unchanged and is displayed at the field's fixed precision. On save, the rounded display value is converted back and the step check applies: for the whole-KiB and whole-MiB fields the display rounds to a whole unit, so the save always lands on a step multiple (the nearest whole unit); for the three 64-KiB-step MB fields the save is rejected unless the rounded display value is itself a step multiple.
interpretations.basis: Follows directly from ADR-028 clause 1: display = bytes / U at fixed precision P and store = round(scaled * U / 10^P) with off-step rejection. The ADR guarantees exact round-trip only at min/default/max, which are all exact step multiples; there is no alternative algorithm consistent with the ADR.
interpretations.impact: An upgraded configuration carrying an off-step 64-KiB-field value must be edited to a step multiple before any settings save succeeds (the persisted value is never silently rewritten); an off-step value in the other four fields is written back as the nearest whole unit on save. Recorded in the changelog task entry and in known_limitations for the 16.6 documentation sweep.

interpretations.question: Where does the explicit step-multiple check live, given that the page is a static embedded resource with no shared runtime with the C# code?
interpretations.chosen: In the settings conversion/validation path: the page's byteLimitToBytes/readByteLimitValues JS plus the native step attributes, and the C# ByteLimitField.TryParseDisplay that the page mirrors. It is deliberately not added to OperationalLimits.Validate or PluginConfigurationValidator.
interpretations.basis: ADR-028 clause 1 requires the check in the settings conversion/validation path and keeps the internal byte-range validation unchanged; the task hard constraint requires the persisted XML to load unchanged (adding it to the server validator would reject an existing off-step in-range XML and fall back to defaults).
interpretations.impact: A non-page client of the elevation-gated configuration POST could still persist an off-step in-range byte value (same as before this task); the page rejects it on the next save, and no new endpoint or exposure is introduced.

known_limitations: The page's inline JavaScript is not executed by any test: the repository deliberately has no JS runtime and none is available in this build environment (node/nodejs/deno/bun/qjs/js/d8/jsc absent; the desktop browser is not connected). The page mapping and algorithm are pinned structurally against the C# mapping; a change to the JS algorithm that preserves the asserted snippets and table would not be caught by a test, and the ADR-028 conversion could only be confirmed live on a real host.

Legacy off-step persisted values: precondition - an ArrTags.xml written by the pre-16.1 page may hold any in-range byte count, e.g. 100000 for ProviderResponseLimitBytes. Behaviour - the value loads, validates, activates, and displays at the field's fixed precision; a save converts the rounded display value back and applies the step check, so for the three 64-KiB-step MB fields the save is rejected until the operator enters a step multiple, and for the whole-KiB/whole-MiB fields the save writes the nearest whole unit. Consequence - an upgrade with such a value must edit that field before any settings save succeeds in the rejected case, and the value is silently adjusted (by at most half a display unit) in the other case; the persisted XML is never rewritten without a save. Recorded in the task 16.1 changelog entry for the 16.6 G6/G8 documentation sweep to consider for the limitations register.

The C# ByteLimitField/ByteLimitUnits mapping has no production caller: the page is a static embedded resource that cannot invoke C#, so the helper is the code-owned contract consumed by the test suite and mirrored by the page. A production-path regression in the page is therefore caught only by the structural tests, not by a shared runtime call.
